mainTopic: Why a מחוסר כפרה may not enter מחנה לויה, and the משנה and ברייתא on when and where a נזיר does his תגלחת הטהרה
overview: The amud opens by finishing אביי's discussion of why someone who has immersed but has not yet brought his קרבנות is held back. A ברייתא shows that even a טמא מת, and even a dead body, may enter מחנה לויה, where the Gate of ניקנור stands. So טומאה cannot be the reason. אביי explains that the real reason is that the person is מחוסר כפרה, still missing his atonement. He learns this from the תורה calling the place 'אהל מועד', which links מחנה לויה to the מקדש. The מקדש rule itself comes from the words 'עוד טומאתו בו'. Then a new משנה describes the תגלחת הטהרה of a נזיר: רבי יהודה says he shaves after the שלמים, and רבי אלעזר says after the חטאת. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל adds that animals brought without names are offered as whatever they fit. The גמרא brings a ברייתא with several readings of 'פתח אהל מועד': it points to the שלמים and not the actual doorway (proved from respect, from רבי יאשיה's קל וחומר, and from רבי יצחק's reading), it sets a time when the doorway is open (אבא חנן), or it excludes a נזירה (רבי שמעון שזורי). רבי שמעון שזורי's teaching continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The Gate of ניקנור has the status of מחנה לויה
steps.stepSummary: אביי sets up his argument by noting that the Gate of ניקנור has the status of מחנה לויה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now, where is the Gate of ניקנור located? In the gates of the לויים, meaning it has the status of מחנה לויה.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי is laying down a basic fact to prepare his next move: the Gate of ניקנור counts as מחנה לויה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People who still owe a קרבן to finish their purification stand at the Gate of ניקנור to bring it. By fixing that this gate is מחנה לויה, אביי moves the question to whether such a person may enter מחנה לויה at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Now consider / after all (opens a line of reasoning)
The Gate of ניקנור, the eastern gate of the עזרה
The Levite camp; in Jerusalem, the הר הבית area

phrases.english: Now, the Gate of Nicanor,
where is it located?
In the gates of the Levites.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues אביי's analysis from before this section, setting up a premise.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The Gate of ניקנור has the status of מחנה לויה.

steps.title: Even a corpse may enter מחנה לויה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a טמא מת, and even a dead body, may enter מחנה לויה, learned from יוסף's bones being 'with' משה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught in a ברייתא: a person who is טמא from a dead body may enter מחנה לויה. And not only a טמא מת, but even the dead body itself, as it says: 'And משה took the bones of יוסף with him.' What does 'with him' mean? With him in his area, with him in מחנה לויה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to knock down the idea that ordinary טומאה keeps someone out of the Gate of ניקנור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If even a dead body may be brought into מחנה לויה, then surely a person who became טמא and has already immersed may enter. So the reason someone must wait before bringing his offering cannot simply be that he may not enter the Gate of ניקנור because of טומאה.

keyTerms.meaning: But it was taught in a ברייתא (introduces a challenge)
A person made impure by contact with a dead body
יוסף's bones, which משה carried out of מצרים
Within his area or boundary

steps.confusionAlert: This is not saying a טמא מת may enter anywhere. He may enter מחנה לויה, but not the מקדש itself (מחנה שכינה).

phrases.english: But it was taught: one impure from a corpse
is permitted to enter the Levite camp,
and not only one impure from a corpse,
but even the corpse itself,
as it is stated: "And Moses took
the bones of Joseph with him."
What is "with him"?
With him within his area,
with him in the Levite camp.
phrases.notes: משה was a לוי, so 'his area' means the camp of the לויים.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא: טְמֵא מֵת מוּתָּר לִיכָּנֵס בְּמַחֲנֵה לְוִיָּיה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the premise of Step 1 (the gate is מחנה לויה) to challenge the idea that טומאה keeps one out of it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that someone waiting to bring his offering is held back because his טומאה stops him from entering the Gate of ניקנור.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If even a dead body may enter מחנה לויה, a person who has immersed certainly may, so being barred from the gate cannot be the reason.

steps.title: The real reason: he is still missing atonement
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that a טבול יום of a זב is treated like a זב and is kept out, because he is מחוסר כפרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, אביי says: one who immersed today from being a זב is considered like a זב. And even so, the reason is that since he is still missing his atonement, he may not enter.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a new explanation: what keeps the person out is not his טומאה but the fact that he has not yet brought his atonement קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי grants that, from the point of view of טומאה alone, such a person could enter מחנה לויה. He still may not enter, because he is מחוסר כפרה. This moves the reason from 'impurity' to 'missing atonement'.

keyTerms.meaning: A person who immersed today and must wait until nightfall to become fully טהור
A man made טמא by a certain kind of bodily discharge
Missing atonement; he has not yet brought the קרבן that completes his purification
He may not enter

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two reasons. אביי's point is that the person is kept out because he is missing atonement, not because of leftover טומאה.

phrases.english: Rather, Abaye says:
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the words in round brackets, since אביי has been the speaker all along.

phrases.english: one who immersed that day from being a zav
is considered like a zav.
And even so,
since he is lacking atonement,
he may not enter.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא (אָמַר אַבָּיֵי): טְבוּל יוֹם שֶׁל זָב כְּזָב דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the challenge in Step 2 by changing the reason for the restriction.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changes the reason: the restriction comes from missing atonement, not from טומאה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The person was kept out of the Gate of ניקנור because of his טומאה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even if his טומאה would allow him in, being מחוסר כפרה keeps him out of מחנה לויה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the idea that being מחוסר כפרה is a separate reason for keeping someone out, apart from טומאה.

steps.title: Why does the תורה call מחנה לויה by the name אהל מועד?
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks why the תורה calls the place where the זב brings his offering 'אהל מועד' if he is really standing in מחנה לויה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he is standing in מחנה לויה, why does the תורה call it 'אהל מועד'?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי raises a question about the wording of the פסוק to set up his source for the rule from Step 3.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the זב brings his offering 'to the entrance of אהל מועד', but in practice he stands at the Gate of ניקנור, which is only מחנה לויה. That gap in wording needs an explanation, and the explanation will be the source for the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: The Tent of Meeting; here it stands for the holiest camp, מחנה שכינה
Why?
Does it call it

phrases.english: And if he is standing in the Levite camp,
phrases.notes: 'He' is the זב, standing at the Gate of ניקנור to bring his offering. ויקרא 15:14 calls that spot 'פתח אהל מועד'.

phrases.english: why does it call it
"the Tent of Meeting"?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי בְּמַחֲנֵה לְוִיָּיה קָאֵי, אַמַּאי קָא קָרֵי לֵיהּ ״אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts finding a source for אביי's rule in Step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the פסוק calls a place in מחנה לויה by the name 'אהל מועד'.

steps.title: מחנה לויה shares the rule of אהל מועד
steps.stepSummary: The name 'אהל מועד' teaches that, just as a מחוסר כפרה may not enter the מקדש, he may not enter מחנה לויה either.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to teach: just as there, in the אהל מועד itself, one missing atonement may not enter, so too in מחנה לויה, one missing atonement may not enter.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers his own question: the תורה uses the name 'אהל מועד' to give מחנה לויה the same rule for a מחוסר כפרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The odd wording becomes a comparison: מחנה לויה is linked to אהל מועד. So the ban on a מחוסר כפרה entering the מקדש carries over to מחנה לויה, which gives a source for אביי's rule in Step 3.

keyTerms.meaning: To say / to teach
Just as there (opens a comparison)
So too

steps.whatToRemember: According to אביי, someone who is מחוסר כפרה may not enter מחנה לויה. This is learned from the תורה calling the place 'אהל מועד', not from his טומאה, since even a טמא מת and a dead body may enter מחנה לויה.

phrases.english: To say: just as there,
phrases.notes: 'There' means the אהל מועד itself, the holiest camp.

phrases.english: one lacking atonement may not enter,
so too into the Levite camp as well,
one lacking atonement may not enter.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמֵימְרָא: מָה הָתָם מְחוּסַּר כַּפָּרָה לָא עָיֵיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 4 and so supports the rule of Step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The name 'אהל מועד' links מחנה לויה to the מקדש, so a מחוסר כפרה is barred from both.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A מחוסר כפרה may not enter מחנה לויה, learned from the comparison to אהל מועד.

steps.title: Where do we learn the rule for the מקדש itself?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that a מחוסר כפרה may not enter the מקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: And there, from where do we know it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא just learned that a מחוסר כפרה may not enter מחנה לויה, because it is compared to the מקדש. Now it asks: how do we know the rule for the מקדש in the first place? This question sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 built the rule for מחנה לויה on top of the rule for the מקדש. That only works if the מקדש rule has its own source. So the גמרא now asks for that base source.

keyTerms.meaning: There. Here it means the מקדש, the place step 5 compared to.
From where do we know it? The גמרא's usual way of asking for a source.

phrases.english: And there, from where do we know it?
phrases.notes: "There" means the מקדש. Step 5 said a מחוסר כפרה can't go in there, and now the גמרא wants the source.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the base rule that step 5 relied on.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק source showing that a מחוסר כפרה may not enter the מקדש.

steps.title: Two phrases in the פסוק include the טבול יום and the מחוסר כפרה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads two phrases of one פסוק. One includes a טבול יום and the other includes a מחוסר כפרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: "He shall be impure" comes to include a טבול יום. "His impurity is still on him" comes to include a מחוסר כפרה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא. The ברייתא learns from extra words in the פסוק that even a טבול יום and a מחוסר כפרה are kept out of the מקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words "his impurity is still on him" tell us that a person can still count as impure for entering the מקדש even after he has fully become טהור. That is the case of the מחוסר כפרה, who has not yet brought his offerings. This gives the base source that step 5's comparison needed.

keyTerms.meaning: To include. A word in the פסוק is read as adding another case to the rule.
Someone who went to the מקוה today but must wait until nightfall to be fully טהור.
Someone who is already טהור but has not yet brought the offerings that complete his purity.

steps.whatToRemember: A מחוסר כפרה is kept out of the מקדש because of "עוד טומאתו בו". Through the comparison in step 5, he is kept out of מחנה לויה too.

phrases.english: As it was taught in a ברייתא:
"He shall be impure" comes to include a טבול יום,
"His impurity is still on him" comes to include a מחוסר כפרה.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The words "עוד טומאתו בו" include a מחוסר כפרה in the ban on entering the מקדש.

steps.title: New משנה: רבי יהודה says to shave after the שלמים
steps.stepSummary: The משנה describes the תגלחת הטהרה. The נזיר brings three animals and, according to רבי יהודה, shaves after slaughtering the שלמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: How is the shaving of purity done? He would bring three animals: a חטאת, an עולה, and שלמים. He slaughters the שלמים and shaves after them. These are the words of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It describes the shaving a טהור נזיר does when his term ends. רבי יהודה says the shaving comes after the שלמים is slaughtered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נזיר who finished his term in purity brings three offerings. The question is which offering's slaughter the shaving should follow. רבי יהודה ties the shaving to the שלמים.

keyTerms.meaning: The shaving of a נזיר who stayed טהור and finished his term.
A sin-offering.
A burnt-offering, which is burned completely.
A peace-offering, which is mostly eaten.

phrases.english: משנה:
The shaving of purity, how is it done?
He would bring three animals:
a sin-offering, a burnt-offering, and a peace-offering.
And he slaughters the peace-offering and shaves after them,
these are the words of רבי יהודה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. It is not connected to the previous discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, the נזיר shaves after the שלמים is slaughtered.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר says to shave after the חטאת
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says the shaving comes after the חטאת, because the חטאת always comes first. After the fact, shaving after any of the three is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר says: He would shave only after the חטאת, because the חטאת comes first everywhere. And if he shaved after any one of the three, he has done his duty.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר disagrees with רבי יהודה. He says the shaving should follow the חטאת. The משנה then adds that, after the fact, shaving after any of the three offerings works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר's reason is a general rule: whenever several offerings are brought together, the חטאת is offered first. So the shaving goes with the first offering. The last line teaches that this order is the right way to do it from the start, but it does not hold back the נזיר after the fact.

keyTerms.meaning: Comes first, goes before.
He has done his duty. It counts.

steps.confusionAlert: "ואם גלח על אחת משלשתן יצא" does not cancel the argument. The argument is about the right way to do it from the start. This line is about after the fact.

phrases.english: רבי אלעזר says:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא הָיָה מְגַלֵּחַ אֶלָּא עַל הַחַטָּאת,
phrases.english: He would shave only after the sin-offering,
because the sin-offering comes first in every place.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם גִּלַּח עַל אַחַת מִשְּׁלׇשְׁתָּן — יָצָא.
phrases.english: And if he shaved after any one of the three of them, he has done his duty.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second opinion against רבי יהודה in step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The shaving should follow the חטאת, but shaving after any of the three is valid after the fact.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: three animals brought without saying which is which
steps.stepSummary: If the נזיר did not say which animal is for which offering, each animal is offered as the offering it is fit for.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: If he brought three animals and did not say which is which, the one fit for a חטאת is offered as a חטאת, the one fit for an עולה as an עולה, and the one fit for שלמים as שלמים.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל adds a separate rule. If the נזיר brought his three animals without naming which is for which offering, we simply match each animal to the offering it fits.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each of the three offerings needs a different kind of animal, so each animal can only fit one offering. Because of that, the נזיר does not have to name them. The kind of animal itself decides which offering it becomes.

keyTerms.meaning: He did not say which animal is for which offering.
The one that is fit for it.

phrases.english: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says:
If he brought three animals and did not say which is which,
the one fit for a sin-offering is offered as a sin-offering,
the one fit for a burnt-offering is offered as a burnt-offering,
the one fit for a peace-offering is offered as a peace-offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a separate case about animals that were brought without being named.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Animals brought without being named are each offered as the offering they are fit for.

steps.title: גמרא: the source for רבי יהודה from "פתח אהל מועד"
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads "פתח אהל מועד" in the נזיר's shaving פסוק as pointing to the שלמים, which also have "פתח אהל מועד" written about them.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The רבנן taught: "And the נזיר shall shave at the entrance of the אהל מועד" — the פסוק is talking about the שלמים, as it says about שלמים, "and he shall slaughter it at the entrance of the אהל מועד".
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins explaining the משנה. It gives the source for רבי יהודה's view that the shaving goes with the שלמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same words, "פתח אהל מועד", appear in the shaving פסוק and in the שלמים פסוק. So the shaving is tied to the slaughtering of the שלמים. That is exactly רבי יהודה's view in the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: The רבנן taught. This opens a ברייתא.
The entrance of the אהל מועד.
The פסוק is talking about...

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that רבי יהודה's view in the משנה is built on how the פסוק is read.

phrases.english: גמרא:
The Sages taught:
"And the nazirite shall shave at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting, etc."
the verse is speaking about the peace-offering,
as it is said: "And he shall slaughter it at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 3:2. That פסוק is about the שלמים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to רבי יהודה's view in step 8 and gives its source.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהודה's view that the shaving follows the שלמים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The shared words "פתח אהל מועד" in במדבר 6:18 and ויקרא 3:2.

steps.title: Maybe it means the real doorway?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks whether "פתח אהל מועד" might mean the actual entrance of the משכן instead of pointing to the שלמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: You say the פסוק is talking about the שלמים. Or maybe it just means the actual doorway of the אהל מועד?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא challenges its own reading from step 11 by suggesting a simpler, literal meaning. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 said "פתח אהל מועד" in the נזיר's פסוק is a hint to the שלמים, because the שלמים also have those words. The obvious objection is that the words may mean exactly what they say: shave at the doorway. The ברייתא raises this before answering it.

keyTerms.meaning: "You say". The ברייתא states its own reading before testing it
Peace offering. One of the נזיר's three קרבנות
Actual, literal
The entrance of the Tent of Meeting

phrases.english: You say the verse is speaking about the peace offering,
or is it only
the actual entrance of the Tent of Meeting?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתָּה אוֹמֵר בִּשְׁלָמִים הַכָּתוּב מְדַבֵּר, אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the reading given in step 11 against a literal alternative.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does "פתח אהל מועד" point to the שלמים, or to the physical doorway?

steps.title: Shaving at the doorway would be disrespectful
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rejects the literal reading: shaving at the entrance of the משכן would be a disgraceful thing to do.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can answer: if so, that would be a disgraceful way to act.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own question. The literal reading cannot be right, because shaving hair at the doorway of the holy place is disrespectful.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof here is based on respect for the מקדש. The תורה would not command something degrading there, so "פתח אהל מועד" must be a hint to the שלמים and not a place to shave.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally "you said". Here it means "you can answer"
If so
A disgraceful, disrespectful manner

phrases.english: You can say: if so,
it is a disgraceful manner.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַרְתָּ: אִם כֵּן דֶּרֶךְ בִּזָּיוֹן הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12 and rejects the literal reading.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The literal reading is impossible because shaving at the doorway would disrespect the מקדש.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא's first reason: shaving at the actual doorway of the משכן would be דרך בזיון, so "פתח אהל מועד" must refer to the שלמים.

steps.title: רבי יאשיה: a קל וחומר from the steps of the מזבח
steps.stepSummary: רבי יאשיה says no logical argument is needed. The תורה bans going up to the מזבח by steps, so it surely bans a disgraceful act like shaving at the doorway.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יאשיה says: That reasoning is not needed. The תורה already said, "Do not go up by steps onto My altar." So all the more so, it forbids a disgraceful act.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יאשיה gives a stronger proof for the same point. He uses a פסוק instead of plain common sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה forbids steps on the מזבח because climbing them is slightly immodest, which is a small disrespect. If even that is forbidden, then shaving hair at the entrance of the משכן, a much bigger disrespect, is surely forbidden. So the "doorway" reading falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not needed. That proof is unnecessary because there is a better source
An argument from a lighter case to a stricter one
Steps
Altar

steps.raayaSupportSource: שמות 20:23, the ban on steps up to the מזבח, applied by קל וחומר.

steps.title: Another version of רבי יאשיה from the מדרש
steps.stepSummary: A bracketed passage quotes a different wording of רבי יאשיה from the מדרש on פרשת נשא. There, the whole derivation is his, and it ends that the פסוק speaks of the שלמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another version, in the מדרש on פרשת נשא: "And the נזיר shall shave". רבי יאשיה says: the פסוק is talking about the שלמים. Or maybe it means the actual doorway? If so, the תורה said "Do not go up by steps...", so all the more so he should not shave at the doorway. Rather, the פסוק is talking about the שלמים.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a side note in brackets showing how the same teaching appears in the מדרש. It is not a new argument, just another wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In our ברייתא, the "disgraceful" reasoning is anonymous and רבי יאשיה adds the steps proof. In the מדרש's version, רבי יאשיה himself asks the question and answers it with the steps קל וחומר. The conclusion is the same: "פתח אהל מועד" points to the שלמים.

Etc. The rest of the quote continues as before

steps.raayaSupportSource: The מדרש on פרשת נשא, using the same steps קל וחומר.

steps.title: רבי יצחק: he only needs to take and place the hair
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק proves it from the פסוק itself. The נזיר only has to "take" his hair and "place" it on the fire, so he must shave right next to the fire of the שלמים, not at the doorway.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק says: That is not needed. The פסוק says, "And he shall take the hair of his נזירות head and put it on the fire..." This describes someone who still has only taking and placing left to do. That leaves out a נזיר who shaved at the doorway, because he still has to take, bring, and place.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק gives a third proof. He reads the wording of the same פסוק closely, without any outside argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק lists only two actions after shaving: taking the hair and putting it on the fire. If he shaved at the doorway, he would need a third action, carrying the hair over to the fire. Since the פסוק leaves that out, he must shave where the שלמים are being cooked.

keyTerms.meaning: Taking (picking up the hair)
Placing (putting it on the fire)
Bringing (carrying it from one place to another)
Lacking, still needing to do

steps.whatToRemember: Three proofs that the נזיר does not shave at the actual doorway: (1) it would be דרך בזיון, (2) רבי יאשיה's קל וחומר from the steps of the מזבח, (3) רבי יצחק: the פסוק mentions only taking and placing, not bringing.

for it says:

and place it on the fire, etc."
phrases.notes: The rest of the פסוק says this fire is under the שלמים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a third, text-based proof for the same conclusion reached in steps 13 and 14.
steps.raayaObject: The נזיר shaves near the fire of the שלמים, not at the doorway of the משכן.
steps.raayaSupportSource: במדבר 6:18, which lists only taking and placing after the shaving, with no bringing.

steps.title: A second version of רבי יצחק's proof
steps.stepSummary: In another version, רבי יצחק himself asks whether the פסוק means the real doorway. He proves from 'and he shall take the hair' that the נזיר shaves where the שלמים are cooked.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say it this way: רבי יצחק says the פסוק is talking about the שלמים. Could it mean the actual doorway of the משכן? No, because the פסוק says 'and he shall take the hair of his נזיר head.' So wherever he cooked the שלמים, that is where he shaved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different version of רבי יצחק's teaching from Step 16. Here he asks the question himself and answers it from the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof is the same as before. The hair only has to be 'taken' and put under the pot, so the shaving happens right by the cooking fire. What changes is the setup: now רבי יצחק asks the doorway question himself, instead of answering a question the ברייתא already asked.

keyTerms.meaning: Some say: introduces a different version of the same teaching
Actual, literal

Cooks (here, the meat of the שלמים)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new opinion that argues with Step 16. It is the same proof by the same רבי יצחק, just told in a different way.

steps.title: אבא חנן: the doorway must be open when he shaves
steps.stepSummary: אבא חנן, in the name of רבי אליעזר, reads 'פתח אהל מועד' as being about time. The נזיר may shave only while the doorway of the משכן is open.
steps.simpleTranslation: אבא חנן says in the name of רבי אליעזר: 'And the נזיר shall shave at the entrance of the אהל מועד' means that as long as the doorway of the אהל מועד is not open, he does not shave.
steps.whatsHappening: A new תנא gives a completely different reading of the words 'פתח אהל מועד.' For him, the words tell us WHEN the נזיר may shave, not WHERE.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier steps asked which place the words point to: the doorway or the spot of the שלמים. אבא חנן changes the question from place to time. The shaving must happen while the משכן's doorway is open.

keyTerms.meaning: In the name of
As long as

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the same words in the פסוק can be read as a rule about time instead of a rule about place.

steps.title: רבי שמעון שזורי: a male נזיר, not a female
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון שזורי starts to explain that 'and the נזיר shall shave' speaks of a male נזיר and not a נזירה. His teaching continues in the next part of the גמרא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון שזורי says: 'And the נזיר shall shave at the entrance of the אהל מועד' means a male נזיר, and not a female נזירה...
steps.whatsHappening: Another תנא begins yet another reading of the same פסוק. He focuses on the word 'הנזיר' and says it leaves out a woman. The sentence is not finished yet; it continues on the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'הנזיר' is in the male form, so רבי שמעון שזורי learns that this shaving at the משכן is for a man and not a woman. His full reason is given in the continuation of his words.
